To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a marker (TG180) that cosegregates with the nematode-resistance gene Mi-3, and we have developed a contig that spans the Mi-3 locus.
we have developed a fine genetic and physical map of the nematoderesistance locus Mi-3 in S. perivivanum and constructed a 600-kb contig spanning the gene in the cultivated tomato S. lycopsericum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new sources of resistance against nematodes, which is of major importance in the breeding of new tomato cultivars.
identifying the molecular basis of resistance to root-knot nematoes in wild tomato species.
the genetic analysis of nematode resistance genes and the identification of molecular markers that can be used for the introgression of these genes in the tomato genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mi-3 gene has been mapped to the S. lycoperiscum BAC clone 2.2, which has been identified in this work.

we have developed a high-resolution genetic map of the region containing the Mi-3 nematode-resistance gene in S. peruvanum and that we have constructed a S. lycopsericum BAC contig spanning the region.
the Mi-3 resistance gene is a single locus that has been mapped in S. lycopericum, and that the gene has been fine-mapped in S. peruviamum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a 600 kb region of S. l. contig that contains Mi-3.
we have developed a set of molecular markers that can be used to introgress the gene Mi-3 into tomato.
we were able to fine map the nematode resistant gene Mi-3 from S. peruvianums to a physical distance of 600 kb.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic maps of S. peruvianium and S. lycopesicum are very similar.
the S. lycopericum genome can be easily mapped using the S. perivivanum genome.
the S. peruviamum genetic map is highly reliable and that the S. lycpersicum genome is highly collinear with that of its wild relative.
